clue.text: Surprised to find a shrub in the sea

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: something found in a place sits inside it, so one piece is placed within the other

parts.note: the Med is the Mediterranean, the sea
a bush is a shrub

explanation.surface: Someone is astonished to come across a bush growing out of the sea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The sea' in crosswords is very often the Med, short for the Mediterranean.
explanation.definitionFit: To be ambushed is to be attacked or caught unawares, so taken by surprise.

clue.text: A lake bird, one of the earliest fliers

parts.note: taken as written
L is the abbreviation for lake on maps
a cock is a male bird

explanation.surface: A water bird on a lake is among the first creatures ever to fly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fliers' tempts you towards birds, but it means aviators: John Alcock and Arthur Brown made the first non-stop transatlantic flight in 1919.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir John Alcock was a pioneering aviator who piloted the first non-stop flight across the Atlantic in 1919.

clue.text: German city in the centre of Hesse, a beautiful state

parts.note: Bonn is a city in Germany, the old West German capital
taken as written

indicators.note: the centre of a word is its middle, so only the middle letters are kept

parts.note: the middle three of the five letters of Hesse

explanation.surface: A German city lies at the heart of the region of Hesse, a lovely German state.
explanation.walkthrough: 'State' looks like a German Land such as Hesse; it means a condition. Bonnie is Scots for pretty.
explanation.definitionFit: Bonniness is the quality of being bonny, that is pretty or attractive, so a condition of good looks.

clue.text: A liking for the organ

definitions.meaning: first meaning: an appetite or inclination
second meaning: the digestive organ of the body

explanation.walkthrough: It reads as a fondness for church music; 'organ' is the body part.
explanation.definitionFit: Stomach means appetite or inclination, as in no stomach for a fight, and is also the body's digestive organ.

clue.text: Make sure there is no right to succeed

indicators.note: there is no says something is absent, so that letter is taken away

parts.note: to ensure is to make sure
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: A lawyer checks that nobody has a legal claim to inherit a title.
explanation.walkthrough: ENSURE without its R gives ENSUE. 'Succeed' means follow on, not win.
explanation.definitionFit: To ensue is to follow on afterwards as a result, which is succeed in its sense of coming next.

clue.text: Tiresome speech —— finish on the floor

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a long, dull piece of talk or writing
second meaning: a levelling layer of cement laid over a concrete base

explanation.surface: A boring speaker is told to wrap up and sit down, or a weary audience slumps to the ground.
explanation.walkthrough: The dash makes it look like one scene; it splits two unrelated meanings of the same word, one from rhetoric and one from building.
explanation.definitionFit: A screed is both a long tedious harangue and the smooth top layer of mortar that builders spread over a concrete base.

clue.text: Get ready to distribute joint, a prepared fix

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to slice a roast so it can be served out
second meaning: a rigged deal, sharing out spoils arranged in advance

explanation.surface: A cook prepares to serve a joint, or someone readies a drug fix.
explanation.walkthrough: The first half is the verb, the second the noun; 'joint' is a roast of meat, not a cannabis cigarette.
explanation.definitionFit: To carve up meat is to cut it for serving, and a carve-up is a dishonest prearranged division, a fix.

clue.text: Number One omitted from choice of two

indicators.note: something omitted from a word is left out of it, so that letter is removed

parts.note: either offers a choice between two
one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: The top choice is dropped from a pair of options.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Number' looks like a figure, but it is numb-er, something that makes you numb. EITHER loses its I.
explanation.definitionFit: Ether was used as an anaesthetic, a substance that numbs, which is the crossword sense of number.

clue.text: In capitals, perhaps, he endlessly made polite representations

definitions.text: In capitals, perhaps, he endlessly made polite representations

parts.note: surface: written in capital letters; setter's reading: posted to capital cities, where embassies are
surface: someone forever drawing or writing politely; setter's reading: an envoy who constantly makes tactful formal protests on his country's behalf

explanation.walkthrough: 'Capitals' suggests letters and 'representations' pictures; both mean the world of embassies and formal diplomatic protests.
explanation.definitionFit: A diplomat is a state's envoy, usually stationed in a foreign capital, whose job is making courteous representations to another government.

clue.text: Duty on watch

parts.note: surface: a tax charged on goods; setter's reading: a soldier's task
surface: a levy on wristwatches; setter's reading: keeping guard

explanation.walkthrough: It reads like customs duty charged on a watch; the duty is a soldier's spell of guarding.
explanation.definitionFit: Sentry-go is the old military term for a sentry's spell of guard duty, pacing back and forth on watch.

clue.text: I love sunshine — crops can produce superb taste

indicators.note: what the letters can produce is something new made out of them, so they are worked into another arrangement

parts.note: taken as written
love is zero in tennis, the letter O
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A farmer muses that a sunny summer gives a harvest of excellent flavour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Taste' suggests flavour of food, but here it means discernment, the refined judgment of an expert.
explanation.definitionFit: Connoisseurship is expert discernment in judging fine things, which is what superb taste means in the sense of refined judgment.

clue.text: Smart endlessly, getting the stick for dishonesty

indicators.note: endlessly says the word has no end, so its final letter is dropped

parts.note: chic means smart or stylish
a cane is a stick

explanation.surface: A well-dressed rogue is caned at school for cheating.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Smart' reads as a description of a person, but it supplies a word for stylish that then loses its tail.
explanation.definitionFit: Chicane is an old noun for trickery or deception, the root of the more familiar chicanery.

clue.text: Instrument once played  the world round

parts.note: taken as written
an orb is a sphere, the world or globe
a round shape is the letter O

explanation.surface: A musical instrument was once played all around the world.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Played the world round' reads as one phrase about worldwide fame; 'played' belongs with the definition, and the rest builds the word piece by piece.
explanation.definitionFit: The theorbo is a large bass lute of the seventeenth century, an instrument no longer in common use.

clue.text: Greatly troubled about a horse's lack of speed

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the stirred letters go round the other piece
troubled means disturbed or stirred up, so the letters are put into disorder

parts.note: taken as written
horse is slang for heroin, abbreviated H

explanation.surface: An owner is badly worried that their racehorse is so slow.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters of GREATLY are rearranged around H. Horse as slang for heroin, and H as heroin, are standard crossword shorthand.
explanation.definitionFit: Lethargy is sluggishness and lack of energy, so a want of speed and vigour.

clue.text: For coloured group of workers, universal recession has such a light effect

definitions.text: universal recession has such a light effect

parts.note: red is a colour
a shift is a group of workers on duty together

explanation.surface: A union says a global economic slump weighs only lightly on a group of workers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Recession' is not economic: it is galaxies receding as the universe expands, and 'light effect' is what happens to their light.
explanation.definitionFit: Red shift is the stretching of light towards longer wavelengths from galaxies moving away, the evidence that the universe is expanding.

clue.text: On the spot for a year, but she passes in poetry

parts.note: a pip is a spot on a playing card or dice
p.a. is per annum, Latin for each year

explanation.surface: Someone stays put for a year while a woman goes by in a poem.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pippa Passes' is a verse drama by Robert Browning in which a girl, Pippa, walks past and changes the lives of those who hear her singing.
explanation.definitionFit: Pippa is the heroine of Browning's poem Pippa Passes, the girl whose passing by is the whole story.

clue.text: Supply part of Australia with friendly sort of society

parts.note: to provide is to supply
NT is the Northern Territory of Australia

explanation.surface: Someone sends goods to an Australian region full of welcoming people.
explanation.walkthrough: A friendly society is a British mutual-aid association, and a provident society is one kind; 'friendly' is that technical term, not mere warmth.
explanation.definitionFit: A provident society is a mutual association for saving against hardship, a type of what Britain calls a friendly society.

clue.text: Guide nail on to wood

parts.note: a brad is a thin flat nail
shaw is an old word for a small wood or thicket

explanation.surface: An instruction to steer a nail into a piece of timber.
explanation.walkthrough: Bradshaw was the famous British railway timetable, a guide to train times from 1839 to 1961.
explanation.definitionFit: Bradshaw's Railway Guide was the standard British book of train timetables, so a Bradshaw is a travel guide.

clue.text: Wines in France may be red or white

definitions.meaning: first meaning: rosés, French pink wines
second meaning: flowers that come in red or white

explanation.walkthrough: 'Red or white' looks like the colours of the wine; it is the flowers, whose red and white versions were the badges of Lancaster and York.
explanation.definitionFit: Rosés are pink French wines, and roses are garden flowers whose blooms are often red or white.

clue.text: Solar panel?

parts.note: surface: powered by the sun; setter's reading: having to do with keeping out sunlight
surface: a photovoltaic panel; setter's reading: a hinged wooden board over a window

explanation.walkthrough: It looks like a device for generating power from sunlight; the question mark warns it is a panel that blocks the sun.
explanation.definitionFit: A shutter is a hinged panel over a window that is closed to keep out light, so it deals with the sun.

clue.text: Stolen earrings first produced in court

parts.note: drops are pendant earrings
hot is slang for stolen goods

explanation.surface: Stolen jewellery turns up as the first exhibit at a trial.
explanation.walkthrough: 'First' tells you the earrings come before the stolen; 'court' is a tennis or squash court, not a law court.
explanation.definitionFit: A drop shot is a softly played stroke that falls just over the net, a shot made on a tennis or squash court.

clue.text: Bill's heart

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a posted notice or label stuck up for display
second meaning: one who sticks at things, a person of perseverance and courage

explanation.walkthrough: It reads as a man called Bill's heart; Bill is a notice, and heart is the staying power of someone who will not give up.
explanation.definitionFit: A sticker is an adhesive label or poster, and also someone who perseveres doggedly, showing the courage called heart.

clue.text: Not a surprise, not even to a member of the Family

parts.note: a number that is not even is odd
a son is one member of a family

explanation.surface: Something comes as no shock, not even to someone in the household.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not even' looks like an intensifier ('not even to him'); it is a number that is not even.
explanation.definitionFit: An odds-on result is the favourite, more likely than not to happen, so it is hardly a surprise.

clue.text: Society  girl and university companion come out

parts.note: a deb is a debutante, a young woman presented in society
OU is the Open University
CH is Companion of Honour, a British order

explanation.surface: A debutante and her college friend make their entrance into society.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Come out' fits the deb's coming-out ball, but it is the definition for a different word.
explanation.definitionFit: To debouch is to emerge from a narrow place into open ground, as troops or a river do.

clue.text: Responsibility for being born handicapped

parts.note: b. is the abbreviation for born in dates
lame means disabled in the leg

explanation.surface: Someone asks who is answerable for a child coming into the world disabled.
explanation.definitionFit: Blame is responsibility for a fault or wrong, the burden of being at fault for something.

clue.text: Epic has preliminary chapter spanning a thousand years

parts.note: CH is the abbreviation for chapter, placed before the other piece as a preliminary
the Iliad is Homer's epic poem

explanation.surface: A long epic poem opens with an introductory chapter covering a millennium of history.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Preliminary' tells you the chapter comes first, ahead of the epic.
explanation.definitionFit: A chiliad is a group of a thousand, especially a period of a thousand years, from the Greek for thousand.

clue.text: Be engaged, but don't look right together

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to fight, as armies engage
second meaning: of colours or clothes, to jar when put side by side

explanation.surface: A couple are betrothed but make an odd-looking pair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Engaged' suggests marriage plans; it means engaged in battle.
explanation.definitionFit: Armies clash when they meet in combat, and colours clash when they look discordant side by side.

clue.text: No light story, that takes us to the tropics from a Pole

definitions.text: No light story, that takes us to the tropics from a Pole

parts.note: surface: a heavy, serious tale; setter's reading: a story set in a place without light

parts.words: takes us to the tropics from a Pole
parts.note: surface: a journey from the North or South Pole; setter's reading: written by a Polish man, Joseph Conrad, and set in tropical Africa

explanation.walkthrough: The capital P on 'Pole' is the giveaway: Joseph Conrad was born in Poland, and his novella travels up the Congo into central Africa.
explanation.definitionFit: Heart of Darkness is Conrad's novella about a voyage into the African interior, a grim story whose title promises no light.

clue.text: Boat turned to one side to let woman embark

indicators.note: to embark is to go aboard, so the woman goes inside the other piece

parts.note: wry means twisted or turned to one side
her stands for a woman

explanation.surface: A boat swings sideways so that a lady passenger can climb on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turned to one side' looks like the boat's manoeuvre, but it is a word meaning twisted, which takes the woman aboard.
explanation.definitionFit: A wherry is a light rowing boat or a broad sailing barge used on rivers to carry passengers or cargo.

clue.text: One man's exquisite pieces are another's jumble

indicators.note: a jumble is a muddle, so the letters of the word before it are mixed up

parts.note: taken as written, ignoring the apostrophe

explanation.surface: A twist on the proverb: what one person thinks fine furniture another sees as junk for a jumble sale.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue echoes 'one man's meat is another man's poison'. A jumble sale is a British charity sale of second-hand goods; the one man is the cabinetmaker Thomas Sheraton.
explanation.definitionFit: Sheraton furniture, named after the eighteenth-century designer Thomas Sheraton, is prized for its elegant, delicate pieces.
